newsitem.title: UNITED NATIONS: More Cyprus talks set for August 11-16 at Geneva.
newsitem.headline: More Cyprus talks set for August 11-16 at Geneva.

text.p: Leaders of the Greek and Turkish Cypriot communities, who on Wednesday began five days of talks on the Cyprus problem, have agreed to hold a second round near Geneva from August 11 to 16, a source close to the negotiations said on Thursday.

The U.N.-sponsored talks between President Glafcos Clerides, who heads the Greek Cypriot community, and Turkish Cypriot leader Rauf Denktash are aimed at reuniting the divided island as a bi-zonal, bi-communal federation.
The first round of talks was opened by Secretary-General Kofi Annan at a rural resort called Troutbeck, 90 miles (145 kms) north of New York City.
Annan said his special adviser for Cyprus, former Ecuadorean Foreign Minister Diego Cordovez, would submit "a number of suggestions" to the two sides to facilitate their work, but gave no details.
After the opening session, the United Nations clamped a news blackout on the proceedings.
Cyprus has been virtually partitioned since troops from Turkey took over the north of the island in 1974 in reaction to a coup in Nicosia backed by the junta then ruling Greece.

A false alarm on Thursday afternoon brought fire fighters rushing to the Sheraton Hotel at Poughkeepsie, a few miles (km) from Troutbeck, where the leaders of most Greek Cypriot political parties are staying, as well as many of Clerides' aides and reporters. The building had to be evacuated.
The hotel's general manager, Donna McLean, told Reuters that "one of the news people on the fourth floor was smoking a cigar and blew smoke up toward the smoke alarm and set it off."
Although there was no fire, safety regulations prevented the hotel from turning off the alarm until the local fire department had checked the hotel, which was back to normal after about 30 minutes.
